explanation: A wire carrying current I through a field B feels a force F = BIL sin(theta), where theta is the angle between the current and the field — this is the 'motor effect' that spins every electric motor. The force is largest when the wire is perpendicular to B (theta = 90 degrees) and drops to zero when the wire lies along the field (theta = 0). Crank up the current, the field, the wire length L, or the angle and watch the pink force arrow grow. The force is perpendicular to both the wire and B, so here it lifts the wire out of the page.
bullets: F = BIL sin(theta): the push is strongest when the wire is at 90 degrees to B.
No force when the current runs parallel to the field (sin 0 = 0).
The force is perpendicular to both the current and the field (the motor effect).
